description.value: An fMRI study of whether individual differences in habitual expressive suppression predict amygdala responses to fearful stimuli under suppression priming in healthy Chinese undergraduates.

spans.text: The functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) study aimed to examine whether individual differences in the tendency to use suppression are correlated with amygdala responses to negative situations when individuals are unconsciously primed with expressive suppression.

description.value: A single-group fMRI study of healthy Chinese undergraduates using a mixed design with instructed fear, suppression-primed and control conditions, and individual-difference measures.

instructions.value: Participants were told that blue and yellow squares represented threat and safe trial types, respectively, and that shocks might occur for one color but not the other, although no shocks were actually delivered. In the spontaneous suppression and watching blocks, they were instructed to attend to the stimulus and their natural feelings. In the synonym matching task, they selected which of two probe idioms was synonymous with the target. After each trial, they rated how negative they felt on a 7-point scale.

spans.text: In the spontaneous suppression and watching blocks, the “attend” cue instructed the participant to view the stimulus and attend to their natural feelings regarding the type of the presented CS.
